The globs are that broad on purpose: a `gh_common.py`-only change has\nto run the `scripts/tests` unit suite that covers it — carried by\n`blueprint-sync` — and under the old three-file glob such a change matched no\narea and ran nothing at all (PR 7 review, F13).\n\n## 4. Manifest schema\n\nBuilt in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then\nposted as the manifest PR comment (§5):\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.json          complete run\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.partial.json  partial run\n```\n\nA run is **partial** when it was given `--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`;\n`--dry-run` writes nothing at all.\n\nStep logs live outside the repository, under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"schema\": 1,\n  \"generator\": \"local/bin/ci.sh\",\n  \"replaces\": \".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml\",\n  \"pr\": 7,                       // GitHub PR number\n  \"branch\": \"issue-7-qpbt-basis\",\n  \"base\": \"main\",                // from the GitHub PR\n  \"base_ref\": \"origin/main\",     // what actually resolved\n  \"merge_base\": \"<sha>\",\n  \"head_sha\": \"<sha>\",           // the SHA every step ran against\n  \"worktree\": \"/abs/path\",\n  \"started\": \"2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800\",   // ISO-8601 with offset\n  \"finished\": \"2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800\",\n  \"seconds\": 1125,               // whole run, integer\n  \"conclusion\": \"success\",       // success | failure | error\n  \"partial\": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict\n  \"areas\": { \"lean\": true, \"blueprint_src\": false, ... },\n  \"changed_files\": [\"MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean\", ...],\n  \"warnings\": [\"texra-blueprint not installed; skipped ...\", ...],\n  \"steps\": [\n    {\n      \"step\": \"build\",           // one of the eight job ids, always all eight\n      \"outcome\": \"success\",      // success | failure | error | skipped\n      \"seconds\": 883,\n      \"log_path\": \"/Users/…/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/0007/<sha>/build.log\",\n      \"blocking\": true,\n      \"note\": \"\"                 // skip reason, exit code, or degradation cause\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nOutcome vocabulary — the distinction is what routes the auto-fix loop:\n\n| `outcome` | Meaning | Auto-fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| `success` | the step ran and passed | — |\n| `failure` | the step ran and the code is wrong | `build` → ci-fix, `blueprint-render` → blueprint-fix, everything else → **never** |\n| `error` | the step could not run (missing tool, unbootstrapped worktree, build lock unavailable) | never — this is an operator problem, not a code problem |\n| `skipped` | gated out, or excluded by `--only` / `--skip-build` | — |\n\n`conclusion` is `failure` if any step failed, else `error` if any step errored,\nelse `success`. The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == \"success\"`.\n\n## 5. Publication\n\nEvidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against\n(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:\n\n* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the\n  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`\n  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish\n  \"absent\" from \"not applicable\";\n* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;\n* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked\n  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.\n\n`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,\nkilled or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the\nreview gate's \"green CI on the same head SHA\" check (invariant 2) fails closed.\nImmediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch\ntip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits\nnonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.\n\nA **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`) publishes nothing at\nall — no statuses, no manifest comment — and keeps its manifest in runtime\nstorage only. `--base` belongs on that list because an overridden base (the PR\nhead, say) can empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success. Partial runs\nare a debugging aid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and\nthey must not clobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.\n\n## 6. Concurrency and locks\n\nTwo advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each\nholds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its\nowner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`\n(default 3 h).\n\n| Lock | Scope | On contention |\n|---|---|---|\n| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |\n| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |\n\nOnly the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and\ntake nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and\ntake nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them\nper-file without serializing.\n\n`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs\n(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —\nthe ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:\nkilling a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.\nSo a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is\nwaited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove\nthe lease directories by hand.\n\n## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache\n\n`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the\nshared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save\npolicy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of\n~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,\nso no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a\nworktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.\n\n1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,\n   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:\n   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a\n   hard error.\n   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);\n     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.\n2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and\n   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never\n   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main\n   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,\n   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`\n   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run\n   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.\n3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at\n   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`. That bootstrap path is where the ProofWidgets\n   prune workaround lives, and a package-free tree is exactly the state that\n   triggers it. `MIPSTARRE_CI_ALLOW_COLD_FETCH=1` overrides for a tree you know\n   is clean.\n4. `lake build`, then `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`, then the\n   comparator drift check.\n\nEvery `lake` and `python3` invocation goes through a subshell that unsets\n`git rev-parse --local-env-vars` first. Inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`\nmake Lake resolve nested package repositories against the wrong repository;\n`.githooks/pre-push:19-24` does the same thing for the same reason, and any\norchestrator that invokes `ci.sh` from inside a git hook inherits the problem.\n\nLake's staleness is trace-hash-based, not mtime-based, so a restored snapshot\nolder than the merge base is safe — but only within one\n`hash(lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, lakefile.toml)` class. Crossing that\nboundary is `build-cache.md`'s problem, not this protocol's: `ci.sh` delegates\nthe check to `warm-worktree.sh` and simply builds whatever it is handed.\n\n## 8. The axiom audit is reported, not run\n\n`blueprint-sync` deliberately has no Lean setup. On GitHub that was forced by\nrepeated runner disk exhaustion, and the job degraded to a `::notice` telling a\nhuman to run the audit locally (`pr-ci.yml:303-317`). Locally the constraint is\ndifferent but the conclusion is the same: the machine has a single full-build\nbudget, already spent by `build`. So `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py` runs, and\nwhen it answers `true` the run records a warning:\n\n> run `python3 scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` in a Lean environment\n\nDe-automation of this kind is a legitimate evolution step (`meta.md` §4), and\nthis one is inherited rather than invented.\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nWhen `build` actually ran (any outcome but `skipped`), one line is appended to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`:\n\n```json\n{\"ts\":\"…\",\"kind\":\"ci-build\",\"trigger\":\"ci.sh pr=0007\",\"seconds\":883,\n \"outcome\":\"success\",\"sha\":\"…\",\"note\":\"branch issue-7-qpbt-basis\"}\n```\n\nThis satisfies the `meta.md` duty that every full build be accounted for, and\nmakes \"how much wall time did CI cost this PR\" answerable by a script. The\nper-step seconds in the manifest are the finer-grained record.\n\n## 10. Trust boundary\n\nTwo things about `ci.sh` are worth stating plainly.\n\n**It executes branch-authored code.** The audit scripts, the test suite, and\n`lakefile.toml` all come from the worktree under test, because that is what CI\nmeans and what the parent workflow did. Never run `ci.sh` on a branch you would\nnot run a shell script from.\n\n**Its logs are untrusted data.** Compiler diagnostics, plasTeX output and test\nfailures can contain arbitrary text, including text shaped like instructions.\n`ci.sh` stores logs verbatim and makes no attempt to clean them. Any consumer\nthat feeds a log into an agent prompt — `autofix.sh` above all — owes the\nsanitization required by invariant 6: strip control characters, break fences,\ntruncate, and frame the payload as data that must not be followed. The manifest\ngives consumers `log_path` rather than log content precisely so this stays the\nconsumer's explicit, visible responsibility.\n\n## 11. Deliberate deviations from the parent workflow\n\n| Parent | Local | Reason |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `::error`/`::notice`/`::warning` | per-step log file + `warnings` array | inert outside Actions; exit codes carry all gating meaning |\n| `cancel-in-progress` for PR runs | second run refused, running builds never killed | local build state is not disposable |\n| cache `restore`/`save` actions | hot-main snapshot read via `warm-worktree.sh`; `ci.sh` never writes the shared cache | invariant 1 — the eviction failure documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142` |\n| `workflow` filter = the YAML file | also `local/bin/ci.sh`, `local/protocols/ci.md` | the CI definition is now three files |\n| `--github-annotations` on the duplicate-helper audit | dropped | annotation-only flag |\n| `push`-to-main and docs-only `pull_request` triggers | none | the docs-only paths existed solely to emit the completion event that started PR Review (`pr-ci.yml:31-33`); locally the lifecycle script calls `review.sh` directly |\n| implicit \"PR event\" job conditions | every run is a PR run | `ci.sh` is only ever invoked on a GitHub PR number |\n\n## 12. Amendments\n\nChanging a gating glob, a step's command set, the manifest schema, the status\ncontexts or their vocabulary, or a lock's name or semantics is an amendment:\nrecord the trigger in `results/telemetry/events.md`, edit this file and\n`ci.sh` together, append to `EVOLUTION.md`, and grep `local/` for every other\nenforcement point (`meta.md` §5). The manifest schema in particular is a\ncontract with `review.sh`, `autofix.sh` and `pr_merge.py`; bump `schema` when\nit changes incompatibly.\n# Build cache protocol — the hot main cache\n\nNormative. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent\nworkflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to\navoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:\n\n| script | role |\n|---|---|\n| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |\n| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |\n| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |\n\nGoverning invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full\n`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,\n`DESIGN.md` wins.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way\n\nThe parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented\nfailure. The load-bearing citations:\n\n| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *\"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere.\"* |\n| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *\"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library.\"* |\n| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *\"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget.\"* |\n| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *\"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache.\"* |\n| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *\"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile.\"* |\n| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |\n| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *\"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could negate the ProofWidgets workaround\"* |\n| Independent cache for the doc subproject | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:135-140` | `docbuild/` is its own Lake project with its own key |\n| Mathlib bumps are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *\"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade\"* |\n| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *\"after repeated runner disk exhaustion\"* |\n\nThe single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable\ncache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the\nsame failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared\nbuild tree.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The two-tier split\n\n`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and\ndifferent sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the\nparent's failure.\n\nAn absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>` for a\none-component branch name. The helper rejects `/`, symlink targets, escape, and\ncanonical overlap with packages, `hot-main`, the repository, or any worktree,\nplus canonical-equal ownership by another worktree. Export it before setup or\nwarming and through dispatch and cleanup; only its target gets `--add-dir`.\n\n**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,\n`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the\nparent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and\ndistributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**\ncopy.\n\n**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The\nparent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud\ncache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once\nper manifest** in a shared, read-only store:\n`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,\nand every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.\n\n> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a\n> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it\n> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any\n> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest\n> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by\n> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old\n> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches\n> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,\n> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key\n> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).\n> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.\n\nConsequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It\nrewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under\nevery published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib\nbumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The cache key\n\n```\nkeyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )\n```\n\nconcatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local\nanalog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in\n`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`\nand `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay\nbyte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.\nA missing input file is a hard error, never a default.\n\nTwo properties matter, and they are not symmetric:\n\n1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's\n   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest\n   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is\n   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash\n   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not\n   need their timestamps preserved.\n2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,\n   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.\n   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`\n   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls\n   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.\n\n---\n\n## 4. On-disk layout\n\nShared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may\nuse `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/\n├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time\n│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose\n├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends\n├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)\n└── hot-main/\n    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this\n    │   └── info\n    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main\n    ├── snapshots/\n    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    │   │   ├── STAMP\n    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build\n    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink\n```\n\nSnapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse\nlexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`\ncalls and no name parsing.\n\n### `STAMP` schema\n\nA flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts\nparse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase\nhex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\n\n```\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\nstatus=complete|partial\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\nwarmer_version=1\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\n                          [--targets \"<lake targets>\"] [--lock-timeout S]\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\n```\n\n### 5.1 Writer lease\n\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\n\nStaleness is decided in this order:\n\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\n\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\nprevent.\n\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\n\n### 5.2 Build\n\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\n   finish, then warm again.\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\n   **No `lake update`.**\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\n   prompts may later read.\n\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\n\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\n\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\n\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\n\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\n\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\n\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\nso loudly.\n\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\"main did not build cleanly\"* —\nnot *\"nothing was published.\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\nreason to retry.\n\n### 5.5 Retention\n\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\n```\n\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\n\nDecision procedure:\n\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\n\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\n\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\n\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\n  clone;\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\n\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\n\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\n\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\n\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\n\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\nlocking there.\n\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\n\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\nwhat a stale lock is.\n\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\n\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\n\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \"no pid, therefore\n  stale\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\n  field is read as \"this host\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\n\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\n\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\n   error.\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\n   if the pin is not already installed.\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the\n   documented failure this check exists to surface.\n6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).\n7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the\n   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed\n   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.\n   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).\n   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the\n   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol\n   exists to prevent.\n8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`\n   calls out `--check` specifically for *\"each fresh worktree used for a PR.\"*\n\n`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero\nif anything is missing.\n\n### 8.1 Git environment hygiene\n\nEvery invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in\n`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every\nvariable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a\nscript invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into\nLake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.\n\n### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround\n\nKept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a\npristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.\n\n*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib\npost-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before\nfetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not\nexist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create\nthe directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.\n\n*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is\n**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.\nRecorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed\nby a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts\ntherefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before\nfetching.\n\n`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete\ndownloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks\na checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from\nsource.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\n\n```jsonc\n{\"ts\": \"<ISO 8601 with offset>\",\n \"kind\": \"warm\" | \"rebuild\" | \"cache-get\",\n \"trigger\": \"<who asked for this>\",\n \"outcome\": \"success\" | \"failed\",\n \"seconds\": <int>,\n \"sha\": \"<commit, when known>\",\n \"note\": \"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\"}\n```\n\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\n\nThree properties are load-bearing:\n\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\n  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.\n* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s\n  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every\n  failure path degrades to a warning.\n* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400\n  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is\n  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Operating procedures\n\n```bash\n# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main\n\n# What is published right now?\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status\n\n# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis\n\n# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check\n\n# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force\n\n# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status\n```\n\nAfter a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm\nfirst, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot\nis invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run\n`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in\neach worktree serialized behind one lock.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades\n\n| condition | behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |\n| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |\n| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |\n| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |\n| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |\n| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |\n| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |\n| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |\n| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |\n| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |\n| `origin/main` does not resolve | Warning, non-zero exit from `--check`, because hooks self-disable silently. |\n| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). Consumer: warning, telemetry skipped. |\n\n---\n\n## 12. Deliberately not ported here\n\n* **Change gating by path filter** (`dorny/paths-filter`) belongs to the local PR\n  CI driver, not to the cache layer. See `local/protocols/ci.md`. Note the parent's\n  documented failure: path filters were patched twice after checks silently never\n  ran, so the driver's globs must stay in lockstep with the audit scripts' scan\n  trees.\n* **The site/badges/docs component store** (`blueprint.yml`, `badges.yml`,\n  `docgen.yml`, `deploy-pages.yml`, `scripts/fetch-latest-artifact.sh`) is a\n  separate concern; `local/bin/site.sh` owns it per `DESIGN.md`.\n* **The `docbuild/` cache** (`docgen.yml:135-140`) is a second, independent Lake\n  project with its own key. Locally the persistent directory *is* the cache: keep\n  `docbuild/.lake/build` in the hot-main checkout and wipe it only when\n  `docbuild/lean-toolchain` or `docbuild/lake-manifest.json` changes, comparing a\n  stored hash exactly as the CI key does. Not implemented by these three scripts.\n* **`create-release.yml`** (toolchain-matched tags) exists purely for the external\n  Lake/Reservoir ecosystem. A local-only setup has no downstream consumers;\n  skipped with that reason.\n* **`update.yml` → a local `mathlib-bump.sh`.** Not built here. When it is, it must\n  end by asking the warmer to build the new toolchain into a fresh snapshot before\n  any agent worktree adopts the bump (§10).\n\n---\n\n## 13. Invariant checklist\n\nA change to any of these scripts must preserve all of the following:\n\n1. Only `cache-warmer.sh` writes into `hot-main/`. Consumers refuse to run there.\n2. `compute_keyhash` is byte-identical across both scripts.\n3. A snapshot becomes visible only via `rename(2)`, fully built and stamped.\n4. `current` is re-pointed only via `rename(2)` over the symlink — never `mv`.\n5. Consumers resolve `current` exactly once per run.\n6. Keyhash mismatch → cold path. Never a partial or best-effort reuse.\n7. Failed builds still publish, flagged `partial`.\n8. GC never removes the snapshot `current` names.\n9. At most one full `lake build` machine-wide; `lake env lean` takes no lock.\n10. `.lake/packages` is a symlink to the read-only store `$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`;\n    the store is `chmod a-w`; no automated `lake update`.\n11. The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround runs before any `lake exe cache get`.\n12. Every `lake` / vendored-`git` invocation goes through `run_outside_git_env`.\n13. `STAMP` is parsed by whitelist and validated; never `eval`ed or `source`d.\n14. Telemetry is best-effort, serialized, sanitized, and lands in the primary checkout.\n15. Every degradation is a loud warning or a hard error. Never a silent no-op.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

This file holds only\nMIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared\nrules never move here.\n\n## Style (MATHLIB_style)\n\n### Linter warnings\n\nDo not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add\nbroad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide\nblocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real\nmaintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.\n\nFix the warning at its source whenever possible:\n\n- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;\n- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass\n  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;\n- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;\n- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than\n  silencing `linter.flexible`.\n\nIf a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting\nexception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably\n`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.\nSuch exceptions should be rare and reviewable. These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n- Cite blueprint nodes by their stable LaTeX label, for example blueprint\n  `lem:cl-concat`. Do not store blueprint line numbers in Lean docstrings. When\n  reviewing, derive the current span with\n  `python3 scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve lem:cl-concat`.\n- Cite paper mirrors by a paper label when one exists, or by a repository path\n  plus a narrow anchored passage when the source has no suitable label. Paper\n  mirror line ranges are acceptable because those mirrors are immutable.\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation Work\n\nIf modifying blueprint material:\n\n- Keep chapter structure under `blueprint/src/chapter/`\n- Ensure `leanblueprint web` succeeds\n- Keep Lean declaration references valid\n- Sync theorem open Lean Elab Command

private def resolveDeclIdent (id : TSyntax `ident) : CommandElabM Name := do
  liftCoreM <| Lean.Elab.realizeGlobalConstNoOverloadWithInfo id

elab "assert_standard_axioms " id:ident : command => do
  let declName ← resolveDeclIdent id
  let axioms := (← Lean.collectAxioms declName).qsort Name.lt
  let expected := #[``propext, ``Classical.choice, ``Quot.sound].qsort Name.lt
  unless axioms == expected do
    throwError
      m!"'{declName}' depends on axioms {axioms.toList}, expected exactly " ++
        m!"{expected.toList}"

elab "assert_no_sorry_axiom " id:ident : command => do
  let declName ← resolveDeclIdent id
  let axioms := (← Lean.collectAxioms declName).qsort Name.lt
  if axioms.contains ``sorryAx then
    throwError m!"'{declName}' unexpectedly depends on `sorryAx`; axioms: {axioms.toList}"

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

root = Path('.')
ordinary_paths = sorted(
    path for path in (root / 'MIPStarRE/LDT').rglob('*.lean')
    if not path.read_text(encoding='utf-8').startswith('module\\n')
)
aggregate = root / 'MIPStarRE/LDT.lean'
meta = root / 'MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean'
owned = ordinary_paths + [aggregate]

assert len(owned) == 85, len(owned)
assert meta in ordinary_paths

def publicize_imports(text: str, *, meta_lean: bool = False) -> str:
    if meta_lean:
        text, count = re.subn(r'"'^import Lean$'"', 'public meta import Lean', text,
                              count=1, flags=re.MULTILINE)
        assert count == 1, count
    return re.sub(r'"'^import '"', 'public import ', text, flags=re.MULTILINE)

def insert_after_module_docstring(text: str, marker: str) -> str:
    start = text.find('/-"'!'"')
    assert start >= 0
    match = re.search(r'"'^-/'"\\n', text[start:], flags=re.MULTILINE)
    assert match is not None
    end = start + match.end()
    return text[:end] + f'\\n{marker}\\n' + text[end:]

for path in ordinary_paths:
    text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    assert text.startswith('import '), path
    if path == meta:
        text = publicize_imports(text, meta_lean=True)
        text = insert_after_module_docstring(text, 'public meta section')
    else:
        text = publicize_imports(text)
        text = insert_after_module_docstring(text, '@[expose] public section')
    path.write_text('module\\n\\n' + text, encoding='utf-8')

text = aggregate.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
assert text.startswith('import ')
aggregate.write_text('module\\n\\n' + publicize_imports(text), encoding='utf-8')

print(f'converted {len(ordinary_paths) - 1} ordinary declaration modules')
print('converted 1 public meta command module')
print('converted 1 pure aggregate module')
print(f'total {len(owned)} paths')
PY

git status --short
printf 'changed files: '
git diff --name-only | wc -l
printf 'module headers: '

from pathlib import Path
import re

root = Path('.')
ordinary_paths = sorted(
    path for path in (root / 'MIPStarRE/LDT').rglob('*.lean')
    if not path.read_text(encoding='utf-8').startswith('module\\n')
)
aggregate = root / 'MIPStarRE/LDT.lean'
meta = root / 'MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean'
owned = ordinary_paths + [aggregate]

assert len(owned) == 85, len(owned)
assert meta in ordinary_paths

def publicize_imports(text: str, *, meta_lean: bool = False) -> str:
    if meta_lean:
        text, count = re.subn(r'"'^import Lean$'"', 'public meta import Lean', text,
                              count=1, flags=re.MULTILINE)
        assert count == 1, count
    return re.sub(r'"'^import '"', 'public import ', text, flags=re.MULTILINE)

def insert_after_module_docstring(text: str, marker: str) -> str:
    start = text.find('/-"'!'"')
    assert start >= 0
    match = re.search(r'"'^-/'"\\n', text[start:], flags=re.MULTILINE)
    assert match is not None
    end = start + match.end()
    return text[:end] + f'\\n{marker}\\n' + text[end:]

for path in ordinary_paths:
    text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    assert text.startswith('import '), path
    if path == meta:
        text = publicize_imports(text, meta_lean=True)
        text = insert_after_module_docstring(text, 'public meta section')
    else:
        text = publicize_imports(text)
        text = insert_after_module_docstring(text, '@[expose] public section')
    path.write_text('module\\n\\n' + text, encoding='utf-8')

text = aggregate.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
assert text.startswith('import ')
aggregate.write_text('module\\n\\n' + publicize_imports(text), encoding='utf-8')
